```{r}
# Data set up

## Below code used to create CSV from API call, but commented out as data already pulled and stored as CSV for faster loading
## write_csv(moviesAll, "Data/TMDB_Movies_1970_2026.csv")

moviesAll <- read.csv("Data/TMDB_Movies_1970_2026.csv", header = TRUE)


# Filter to only non obscure English movies
moviesClean <- moviesAll %>%
  filter(
    revenue > 0,
    budget > 0,
    original_language == "en"
  )

str(moviesAll)

range(moviesAll$vote_count, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create sequel dataframe with days until sequel and collection name
moviesSequel <- moviesClean %>%
  mutate(release_date = as.Date(release_date)) %>%
  
  # first, create a column for next_release_date for movies in collections only
  group_by(collection_name) %>%
  arrange(release_date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    next_release_date = if (!is.na(collection_name[1])) lead(release_date) else NA
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  # calculate days_until_sequel safely
  mutate(
    days_until_sequel = ifelse(
      !is.na(next_release_date) & !is.na(release_date),
      as.numeric(difftime(next_release_date, release_date, units = "days")),
      NA
    )
  )

moviesSequel <- moviesSequel %>%
  group_by(collection_name) %>%
  arrange(release_date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    sequel_number = ifelse(is.na(collection_name), 1, row_number()),
    sequel_cat = case_when(
      sequel_number >= 4 ~ ">3",
      TRUE ~ as.character(sequel_number)
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

moviesSequel$sequel_cat <- factor(moviesSequel$sequel_cat,levels = c("1", "2", "3", ">3"))

# Find the number of movies in each collection (collections may be NA)
collection_counts <- moviesSequel %>%
  group_by(collection_name) %>%
  summarise(count = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(count))

# Find each individual genre and count how many movies in each genre (genres may be comma delimited)
genre_counts <- moviesSequel %>%
  filter(!is.na(genres)) %>%
  separate_rows(genres, sep = ", ") %>%
  group_by(genres) %>%
  summarise(count = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(count))

# Add flag for each genre in genre_counts
moviesSequel <- moviesSequel %>%
  mutate(
    is_action = ifelse(grepl("Action", genres), 1, 0),
    is_adventure = ifelse(grepl("Adventure", genres), 1, 0),
    is_animation = ifelse(grepl("Animation", genres), 1, 0),
    is_comedy = ifelse(grepl("Comedy", genres), 1, 0),
    is_crime = ifelse(grepl("Crime", genres), 1, 0),
    is_documentary = ifelse(grepl("Documentary", genres), 1, 0),
    is_drama = ifelse(grepl("Drama", genres), 1, 0),
    is_family = ifelse(grepl("Family", genres), 1, 0),
    is_fantasy = ifelse(grepl("Fantasy", genres), 1, 0),
    is_history = ifelse(grepl("History", genres), 1, 0),
    is_horror = ifelse(grepl("Horror", genres), 1, 0),
    is_music = ifelse(grepl("Music", genres), 1, 0),
    is_mystery = ifelse(grepl("Mystery", genres), 1, 0),
    is_romance = ifelse(grepl("Romance", genres), 1, 0),
    is_science_fiction = ifelse(grepl("Science Fiction", genres), 1, 0),
    is_tv_movie = ifelse(grepl("TV Movie", genres), 1, 0),
    is_thriller = ifelse(grepl("Thriller", genres), 1, 0),
    is_war = ifelse(grepl("War", genres), 1, 0),
    is_western = ifelse(grepl("Western", genres), 1, 0)
  )

genre_vars <- c(
  "is_action", "is_adventure", "is_animation", "is_comedy", "is_crime",
  "is_documentary", "is_drama", "is_family", "is_fantasy", "is_history",
  "is_horror", "is_music", "is_mystery", "is_romance",
  "is_science_fiction", "is_thriller", "is_war", "is_western"
)

genre_summary <- data.frame(

  # how many movies are in each genre
  count = sapply(genre_vars, function(g) sum(moviesSequel[[g]], na.rm = TRUE)),

  # % of all movies that belong to this genre
  genre_percent = sapply(genre_vars, function(g)
    sum(moviesSequel[[g]], na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(moviesSequel) * 100
  ),

  # % of movies in this genre that get sequels
  sequel_percent = sapply(genre_vars, function(g) {
    denom <- sum(moviesSequel[[g]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (denom == 0) return(NA_real_)

    num_with_sequel <- sum(
      moviesSequel[[g]] == 1 &
      !is.na(moviesSequel$days_until_sequel),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    num_with_sequel / denom * 100
  })
)

genre_matrix <- moviesSequel[, genre_vars]
genre_cor <- cor(genre_matrix)

# Create years column by dividing days_until_sequel by 365.25 to account for leap years
moviesSequel$months_until_sequel <- moviesSequel$days_until_sequel / 30.44
moviesSequel$years_until_sequel <- moviesSequel$days_until_sequel / 365.25
moviesSequel$decade <- (as.integer(format(moviesSequel$release_date, "%Y")) %/% 10) * 10

# Create survival data
moviesSequel$censor <- ifelse(is.na(moviesSequel$days_until_sequel), 0, 1)
moviesSequel$time <- ifelse(is.na(moviesSequel$days_until_sequel), as.Date("2026-2-26") - moviesSequel$release_date, moviesSequel$days_until_sequel)

# Read in CPI data to get CPI adjusted revenue and budget
CPI <- read_csv("C:/Users/zmose/OneDrive/Desktop/Data Sets/CPI1970-2026.csv", na ="NA")

#Get year and month from date column and create year_month column
CPI <- CPI %>%
  mutate(year = as.numeric(format(as.Date(observation_date, format="%Y-%m-%d"), "%Y")),
       month = as.numeric(format(as.Date(observation_date, format="%Y-%m-%d"), "%m")),
       year_month = paste(year, month, sep="-"))
moviesSequel <- moviesSequel %>%
  mutate(release_year = as.numeric(format(release_date, "%Y")),
         release_month = as.numeric(format(release_date, "%m")),
         release_year_month = paste(release_year, release_month, sep="-"))

#Add CPIAUCSL column to moviesSequel by matching release_year_month with year_month in CPI
moviesSequel <- moviesSequel %>%
  left_join(
    dplyr::select(CPI, year_month, CPIAUCSL),
    by = c("release_year_month" = "year_month")
  )
base_cpi <- CPI %>%
  filter(observation_date <= as.Date("2026-02-26")) %>%
  arrange(desc(observation_date)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  pull(CPIAUCSL)
moviesSequel <- moviesSequel %>%
  mutate(
    CPIAdjustedRevenue = ifelse(!is.na(revenue) & !is.na(CPIAUCSL),
                            revenue * (base_cpi / CPIAUCSL),
                            NA_real_),
    CPIAdjustedBudget = ifelse(!is.na(budget) & !is.na(CPIAUCSL),
                            budget * (base_cpi / CPIAUCSL),
                            NA_real_)
  )

# Create survival object using time and censor columns
moviesSequel <- moviesSequel %>%
  mutate(response = Surv(time, censor))

# Check structure of moviesSequel to all columns are correct
str(moviesSequel)


# Remove all movies released after 2019
moviesSequel2 <- moviesSequel %>%
  filter(release_date <= as.Date("2019-12-31"))

# See rates of sequels at particular cut offs
cuts <- quantile(moviesSequel2$CPIAdjustedRevenue, probs = seq(0.1, 0.9, 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
data.frame(
  cutoff = cuts,
  n_movies = sapply(cuts, function(cut) {
    sum(moviesSequel2$CPIAdjustedRevenue > cut, na.rm = TRUE)
  }),
  sequel_rate = sapply(cuts, function(cut) {
    df <- moviesSequel2 %>% filter(CPIAdjustedRevenue > cut)
    mean(!is.na(df$days_until_sequel)) * 100
  })
)


# One final filter to only include movies with CPI adjusted revenue greater than 10 million and CPI adjusted budget greater than 10 thousand IF they don't have any sequels
moviesFinal <- moviesSequel2 %>%
  filter(
    CPIAdjustedRevenue > 100000000 & CPIAdjustedBudget > 15000
  )

# Percent of days_until_sequel that are not NA
sum(!is.na(moviesFinal$days_until_sequel)) / nrow(moviesFinal) * 100

sequelPercentageFinal<-moviesFinal %>%
  summarise(
    action_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_action == 1) / sum(is_action == 1) * 100,
    adventure_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_adventure == 1) / sum(is_adventure == 1) * 100,
    animation_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_animation == 1) / sum(is_animation == 1) * 100,
    comedy_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_comedy == 1) / sum(is_comedy == 1) * 100,
    crime_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_crime == 1) / sum(is_crime == 1) * 100,
    documentary_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_documentary == 1) / sum(is_documentary == 1) * 100,
    drama_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_drama == 1) / sum(is_drama == 1) * 100,
    family_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_family == 1) / sum(is_family == 1) * 100,
    fantasy_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_fantasy == 1) / sum(is_fantasy == 1) * 100,
    history_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_history == 1) / sum(is_history == 1) * 100,
    horror_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_horror == 1) / sum(is_horror == 1) * 100,
    music_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_music == 1) / sum(is_music == 1) * 100,
    mystery_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_mystery == 1) / sum(is_mystery == 1) * 100,
    romance_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_romance == 1) / sum(is_romance == 1) * 100,
    science_fiction_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_science_fiction == 1) / sum(is_science_fiction == 1) * 100,
    tv_movie_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_tv_movie == 1) / sum(is_tv_movie == 1) * 100,
    thriller_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_thriller == 1) / sum(is_thriller == 1) * 100,
    war_percent = sum(!is.na(days_until_sequel) & is_war == 1) / sum(is_war == 1)
  )

# Find the number of movies in each collection (collections may be NA)
collection_counts2 <- moviesFinal %>%
  group_by(collection_name) %>%
  summarise(count = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(count))

moviesFit <- survfit(response ~ 1, data = moviesFinal)

year_lines <- seq(365, max(moviesFinal$time, na.rm = TRUE), by = 365)
decade_lines <- seq(3650, max(moviesFinal$time, na.rm = TRUE), by = 3650)
survfit2(Surv(time, censor) ~ 1, data = moviesFinal) %>%
  ggsurvfit() +
  labs(
    title = "Kaplan-Meier Survival Curve for Time Until Sequel",
    x = "Time (days)",
    y = "Survival Probability"
  ) +
  add_confidence_interval() +
  add_risktable() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = year_lines, linetype = "dotted", color = "lightgrey") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = decade_lines, linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgrey") +
  theme_classic()

plot(moviesFit,
     conf.int = TRUE,
     main = "Kaplan-Meier Survival Curve for Time Until Sequel",
     xlab = "Time (days)",
     ylab = "Survival Probability",
     lwd=3)

# Light grey yearly lines
for (t in seq(365, max(moviesFit$time), by = 365)) {
  abline(v = t, col = "grey90", lty = 3)
}

# Darker grey lines every 10 years
for (t in seq(3650, max(moviesFit$time), by = 3650)) {
  abline(v = t, col = "grey60", lty = 2, lwd = 1.2)
}

plot(moviesFit,
     conf.int = FALSE,
     fun = "cumhaz",
     main = "Cumulative Hazard Function for Time Until Sequel",
     xlab = "Time (days)",
     ylab = "Cumulative Hazard",
     lwd=3)

# Light grey yearly lines
for (t in seq(365, max(moviesFit$time), by = 365)) {
  abline(v = t, col = "grey90", lty = 3)
}

# Darker grey lines every 10 years
for (t in seq(3650, max(moviesFit$time), by = 3650)) {
  abline(v = t, col = "grey60", lty = 2, lwd = 1.2)
}

haz <- muhaz(moviesFinal$time, moviesFinal$censor)
plot.muhaz(haz,
           main = "Smoothed Hazard Function for Time Until Sequel",
           xlab = "Time (days)", ylab = "Hazard Rate")
lines(haz, lwd = 3)

# Light grey yearly lines
for (t in seq(365, max(moviesFit$time), by = 365)) {
  abline(v = t, col = "grey90", lty = 3)
}

# Darker grey lines every 10 years
for (t in seq(3650, max(moviesFit$time), by = 3650)) {
  abline(v = t, col = "grey60", lty = 2, lwd = 1.2)
}

#Find movie sequels with time = 0
moviesFinal %>%
  filter(time <= 1) %>%
  dplyr::select(title, time, release_date, next_release_date, collection_name)


moviesFinal <- moviesFinal %>%
  mutate(
    revenue_mil = revenue / 1e6,
    budget_mil = budget / 1e6,
    CPIAdjustedRevenue_tmil = CPIAdjustedRevenue / 1e7,
    CPIAdjustedBudget_mil = CPIAdjustedBudget / 1e6,
    vote_count_k = vote_count / 1e3,
    runtime_hr = runtime / 60,

    log_budget = log(CPIAdjustedBudget_mil),
    log_revenue = log(CPIAdjustedRevenue_tmil)
  )

summary(moviesFinal)


# For SAS export
write.csv(moviesFinal, "moviesFinal.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Category analysis

# PCA Analysis

X <- moviesFinal[, genre_vars]
pca_fit <- prcomp(X, scale. = TRUE)
summary(pca_fit)
plot(pca_fit, type = "l", main = "Scree Plot")

loadings <- pca_fit$rotation
round(loadings[,1:5], 2)
##PC1: Light vs dark tone
##PC2: Action/sci-fi vs romance/drama
##PC3: Historical seriousness vs horror/mystery
##PC4: Romance/comedy vs historical content
##PC5: Crime realism vs horror/sci-fi
round(loadings[,1:4], 2)
##PC1: Genre intensity spectrum (family/comedy/animation vs thriller/crime/drama)
##PC2: Action/sci-fi spectacle vs romance/drama narratives
##PC3: Historical/war context vs horror/mystery genres
##PC4: Romance/comedy orientation vs structured/historical content

## Above PC analysis creates bins of genres with too little overlap. Attempting to reorganize based on correlations

genre_matrix <- moviesFinal[, genre_vars]
co_matrix <- t(genre_matrix) %*% as.matrix(genre_matrix)
overlap_matrix <- co_matrix / diag(co_matrix)

high_overlap <- which(overlap_matrix > 0.5 & overlap_matrix < 1, arr.ind = TRUE)

# Convert to readable pairs
overlap_pairs <- data.frame(
   genre1 = rownames(overlap_matrix)[high_overlap[,1]],
   genre2 = colnames(overlap_matrix)[high_overlap[,2]],
   overlap = overlap_matrix[high_overlap])

# Sort by strongest overlap
overlap_pairs <- overlap_pairs[order(-overlap_pairs$overlap), ]

overlap_pairs

genre_vars <- c(
  "is_action","is_adventure","is_animation","is_comedy","is_crime",
  "is_documentary","is_drama","is_family","is_fantasy","is_history",
  "is_horror","is_music","is_mystery","is_romance",
  "is_science_fiction","is_thriller","is_war","is_western"
)

# Reorganizing the genre bins for each

dist_mat <- as.dist(1 - overlap_matrix)
hc <- hclust(dist_mat, method = "average")
clusters <- cutree(hc, k = 5)
genre_clusters <- data.frame(
   genre = names(clusters),
   cluster = clusters
)
genre_clusters

moviesFinal <- moviesFinal %>%
  mutate(
    genre_action = ifelse(
      is_action + is_crime + is_science_fiction + is_thriller > 0, 1, 0
    ),
    genre_entertainment = ifelse(
      is_adventure + is_animation + is_comedy + is_family +
      is_fantasy + is_music + is_western > 0, 1, 0
    ),
    genre_drama = ifelse(
      is_drama + is_history + is_romance + is_war > 0, 1, 0
    ),
    genre_horror = ifelse(
      is_horror + is_mystery > 0, 1, 0
    ),
    genre_documentary = ifelse(
      is_documentary > 0, 1, 0
    )
  )

CoxFit2 <- coxph(response ~ runtime_hr + vote_average + vote_count + popularity + cast_size + is_action + is_adventure + is_animation + is_comedy + is_crime + is_documentary + is_drama + is_family + is_fantasy + is_history + is_horror + is_music + is_mystery + is_romance + is_science_fiction +is_thriller + is_war + is_western + factor(decade) + log_budget + log_revenue + strata(factor(sequel_cat)), ties = "breslow", data = moviesFinal)

CoxFitGenreBins <- coxph(response ~ runtime_hr + vote_average + vote_count + popularity + cast_size + genre_action + genre_entertainment + genre_drama + genre_horror + genre_documentary + factor(decade) + log_budget + log_revenue + strata(factor(sequel_cat)), ties = "breslow", data = moviesFinal)

lrtest(CoxFitGenreBins, CoxFit2)
AIC(CoxFitGenreBins)
AIC(CoxFit2)
```


```{r}
# ATF
ExpFit <- flexsurvreg(Surv(time, censor) ~ 1, dist = "exponential", data = moviesFinal)
WeiFit <- flexsurvreg(Surv(time, censor) ~ 1, dist = "weibull", data = moviesFinal)

                       dist = "gengamma",
                       data = moviesFinal)

summary(fullFit)

make_group_data <- function(df, group_val) {
  subset_df <- df[df$sequel_cat == group_val, ]

  data.frame(
    runtime_hr = mean(subset_df$runtime_hr, na.rm = TRUE),
    vote_average = mean(subset_df$vote_average, na.rm = TRUE),
    vote_count_k = mean(subset_df$vote_count_k, na.rm = TRUE),
    popularity = mean(subset_df$popularity, na.rm = TRUE),
    cast_size = mean(subset_df$cast_size, na.rm = TRUE),

    is_action = mean(subset_df$is_action, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_adventure = mean(subset_df$is_adventure, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_animation = mean(subset_df$is_animation, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_comedy = mean(subset_df$is_comedy, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_crime = mean(subset_df$is_crime, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_documentary = mean(subset_df$is_documentary, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_drama = mean(subset_df$is_drama, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_family = mean(subset_df$is_family, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_fantasy = mean(subset_df$is_fantasy, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_history = mean(subset_df$is_history, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_horror = mean(subset_df$is_horror, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_music = mean(subset_df$is_music, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_mystery = mean(subset_df$is_mystery, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_romance = mean(subset_df$is_romance, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_science_fiction = mean(subset_df$is_science_fiction, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_thriller = mean(subset_df$is_thriller, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_war = mean(subset_df$is_war, na.rm = TRUE),
    is_western = mean(subset_df$is_western, na.rm = TRUE),

    decade = median(subset_df$decade, na.rm = TRUE),

    log_budget = mean(subset_df$log_budget, na.rm = TRUE),
    log_revenue = mean(subset_df$log_revenue, na.rm = TRUE),

    sequel_cat = factor(group_val, levels = levels(df$sequel_cat))
  )
}

newdata <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(moviesFinal$sequel_cat),
                                 function(g) make_group_data(moviesFinal, g)))

cols <- 1:4
plot(km_fit,
     col = cols,
     lwd = 2,
     lty = 1,
     xlab = "Time in Days",
     ylab = "Survival Probability",
     main = "KM vs AFT Survival by Sequel Category")
lines(fullFit,
      newdata = newdata,
      col = cols,
      lwd = 2,
      lty = 2,
      ci = FALSE)
legend("bottomleft",
       legend = levels(moviesFinal$sequel_cat),
       col = cols,
       lwd = 2,
       lty = 1,
       title = "KM (solid) vs AFT (dashed)",
       cex = 0.5)

plot(km_fit,
     fun = "cumhaz",
     col = cols,
     lwd = 2,
     lty = 1,
     xlab = "Time in Days",
     ylab = "Cumulative Hazard",
     main = "KM vs AFT Cumulative Hazard by Sequel Category")
lines(fullFit,
      newdata = newdata,
      type = "cumhaz",
      col = cols,
      lwd = 2,
      lty = 2,
      ci = FALSE)
legend("right",
       legend = levels(moviesFinal$sequel_cat),
       col = cols,
       lwd = 2,
       lty = 1,
       title = "KM (solid) vs AFT (dashed)",
       cex = 0.5)

# Plots show that the ATF model is probably not the best fit for the data, as the predicted cumulative hazard and survival curves do not align well with the Kaplan-Meier estimates. ATF model is likely overfitting the data with too many covariates and not capturing the underlying hazard function accurately. The predicted cumulative hazard curve is much steeper than the Kaplan-Meier estimate, and the predicted survival curve drops much more quickly than the Kaplan-Meier curve, indicating that the model may be overestimating the hazard of a sequel occurring. Will likely need to use Cox PH model to better capture the effects of covariates on the hazard of a sequel occurring without making strong assumptions about the baseline hazard function.
```

```{r}
#Cox Model

CoxFit <- coxph(response ~ runtime_hr + vote_average + vote_count_k + popularity + cast_size + is_action + is_adventure + is_animation + is_comedy + is_crime + is_documentary + is_drama + is_family + is_fantasy + is_history + is_horror + is_music + is_mystery + is_romance +is_science_fiction + is_thriller + is_war + is_western + decade + log_budget + log_revenue + strata(factor(sequel_cat)),
                ties = "breslow",
                data = moviesFinal)

CoxFit2 <- coxph(response ~ runtime_hr + vote_average + vote_count_k + popularity + cast_size + is_action + is_adventure + is_animation + is_comedy + is_crime + is_documentary + is_drama + is_family + is_fantasy + is_history + is_horror + is_music + is_mystery + is_romance + is_science_fiction +is_thriller + is_war + is_western + factor(decade) + log_budget + log_revenue + strata(factor(sequel_cat)),
                 ties = "breslow",
                 data = moviesFinal)

lrtest(CoxFit, CoxFit2)

summary(CoxFit2)

stepAIC(CoxFit2, trace=FALSE)

CoxFinal <- coxph(response ~ runtime + vote_count_k + cast_size + 
    is_action + is_animation + is_drama + is_horror + is_music + 
    is_romance + is_science_fiction + is_thriller + is_war + 
    factor(decade) + log_budget + log_revenue + strata(factor(sequel_cat)), 
    data = moviesFinal, ties = "breslow")

summary(CoxFinal)

plot(survfit(CoxFinal),
     lwd = 2,
     mark.time = FALSE,
     conf.int = FALSE,
     col = 1:length(survfit(CoxFinal)$strata),
     main = "Stratified Cox Model Baseline Survival by Sequel Category",
     xlab = "Time (Days)",
     ylab = "Survival Probability")

legend("bottomleft",
       legend = names(survfit(CoxFinal)$strata),
       col = 1:length(survfit(CoxFinal)$strata),
       lwd = 2)

plot(survfit(CoxFinal),
     lwd = 2,
     mark.time = FALSE,
     conf.int = FALSE,
     col = 1:length(survfit(CoxFinal)$strata),
     fun = "cumhaz",
     main = "Stratified Cox Model: Cumulative Hazard by Sequel Category",
     xlab = "Time (Days)",
     ylab = "Cumulative Hazard")

legend("right",
       legend = names(survfit(CoxFinal)$strata),
       col = 1:length(survfit(CoxFinal)$strata),
       lwd = 2)


phcheck <- cox.zph(CoxFinal)
phcheck
#Iterate through each variable and plot Schoenfield residuals
vars <- rownames(phcheck$table)
vars <- vars[vars != "GLOBAL"]
for (i in seq_along(vars)) {
  plot(phcheck, var = i, main = paste("Schoenfeld Residual Plot for", vars[i]))
  abline(h = 0, lty = 3)
}

CoxFinal2 <- coxph(response ~ runtime_hr + vote_count_k + cast_size + is_action + is_animation + is_drama + is_horror + is_music + is_romance + is_science_fiction + is_thriller + is_war +factor(decade) + log_budget + log_revenue + strata(factor(sequel_cat)) + tt(vote_count_k) + tt(is_animation),data = moviesFinal, ties = "breslow", tt = function(x, t, ...) x * log(t))

CoxFinal3 <- coxph(response ~ runtime_hr + vote_count_k + cast_size + is_action + is_animation + is_drama + is_horror + is_music + is_romance + is_science_fiction + is_thriller + is_war +factor(decade) + log_budget + log_revenue + strata(factor(sequel_cat)) + tt(vote_count_k) + tt(is_animation) + tt(log_budget) + tt(log_revenue),data = moviesFinal, ties = "breslow", tt = function(x, t, ...) x * log(t))

lrtest(CoxFinal, CoxFinal2)
lrtest(CoxFinal3, CoxFinal2)

stepAIC(CoxFinal3)
# Final model is CoxFinal2, which includes time-varying effects for vote_count_k and is_animation, as these were the only two variables that showed significant violations of the proportional hazards assumption.
```

#Cure model

cure_model <- smcure(
  Surv(time, censor) ~ runtime_hr + vote_count + cast_size +
    is_action + is_animation + is_drama + is_horror + is_music +
    is_romance + is_science_fiction + is_thriller + is_war +
    factor(decade) + log_budget + log_revenue,

  cureform = ~ runtime_hr + vote_count + cast_size +
    is_action + is_animation + is_drama + is_horror + is_music +
    is_romance + is_science_fiction + is_thriller + is_war +
    factor(decade) + log_budget + log_revenue,

  data = moviesFinal,
  model = "ph"
)

# Outlier analysis

dfb <- residuals(CoxFinal, type="dfbetas")
ldresids <- residuals(CoxFinal, type="deviance")
colnames(dfb) <- paste0("dfbeta_", names(coef(CoxFinal)))
moviesFinal2 <- moviesFinal %>%
  dplyr::select(id, title, everything()) %>%
